title: How a Mop and a Broom Became a Powerful Picture: The Gordon Parks Story
summary: What if a simple photo could change how people see the world? Gordon Parks believed it could. He was a photographer who used his camera to fight against racism and unfairness. This September, a gallery in New York City will open an exhibition called “Voices in the Mirror” to honor his incredible work — and it’s also the 20th birthday of The Gordon Parks Foundation, a group that keeps his legacy alive. Parks was born in 1912 and grew up in a time when Black Americans faced terrible discrimination, especially in the South. He first picked up a camera in 1937 after seeing photos that showed real American life. He said, “I saw that the camera could be a weapon against poverty, against racism, against all sorts of social wrongs. I knew at that point I had to have a camera.” And he was right! In 1942, he became the first Black photographer hired by the Farm Security Administration, a government program. He was sent to Washington, D.C., where he said discrimination was worse than anywhere he’d ever seen. One of his most famous photos is called “American Gothic, Washington, D.C.” It shows a woman named Ella Watson standing stiffly with a mop and broom in front of an American flag. The pose copies a famous painting called “American Gothic” from 1930, but Parks’ version tells a very different story. After talking with Watson about her hard life, Parks wanted to show the truth about America in 1942. He said, “I didn’t care about what anybody else felt. That’s what I felt about America and Ella Watson’s position inside America.” The exhibition also includes photos of famous people like Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X, plus everyday families. Some people in the photos, like Malcolm X’s daughter, will share their memories. The show runs from September 18 to November 7. If you love stories about real heroes, this is one to see!
why_it_matters: Just as Gordon Parks used a camera to shine a light on injustice, you can use your own words, art, or actions to stand up for what is right in your school or community.

background_read: The Farm Security Administration (a U.S. government agency) was created during the Great Depression to help farmers and also hired photographers to show what life was like around the country.
The original painting ‘American Gothic’ by Grant Wood shows a stern farmer and his daughter and became a symbol of rural America.
Gordon Parks later became the first Black director of a major Hollywood movie with the film ‘Shaft,’ which helped start a whole new style of action movies.

perspectives.description: Many see the photo as a powerful statement against racism, showing how one simple image can start big conversations.
Some believe it is important to preserve these photographs so that future generations can learn from the past.
A few argue that a single image cannot fix deep-rooted problems, but admit it can still make people think differently.
